# Structure

**You are in FlipperWiki** - the wiki for whoever is at the glass: one page per thing a player can point at, compiled by an LLM out of rule files cut one at a time from the documents next door. The only repository here with prose of its own, and nothing under wiki/ is written by a person.

The Space Train (MAC, 1987) project is 14 repositories. This table is generated into all of them, so that each one knows the others.

| Repository | What it holds | This repository | Remote |
|---|---|---|---|
| [FlipperArchitecture](../FlipperArchitecture) | the machine itself: the masterplan spreadsheet, the 1987 flyers, the photographs, and the documents that describe the cabinet rather than any software driving it | no direct link | [SpaceTrainMac/FlipperArchitecture](https://github.com/SpaceTrainMac/FlipperArchitecture) |
| [FlipperEngine](../FlipperEngine) | the Master Control Program: the engine and the game rules that run the cabinet on a Raspberry Pi, and the documents in docs/ | no direct link | [SpaceTrainMac/FlipperEngine](https://github.com/SpaceTrainMac/FlipperEngine) |
| [FlipperSimulator](../FlipperSimulator) | the cabinet in a browser: the decoder, the HTTP layer, the page and their tests. It builds the engine checkout beside it, as it is on disk | no direct link | [SpaceTrainMac/FlipperSimulator](https://github.com/SpaceTrainMac/FlipperSimulator) |
| [FlipperVPX](../FlipperVPX) | the cabinet with a ball in it: the Visual Pinball X plugin that runs the engine against a physics simulator, the bridge it drives, and the generators that draw the table and the backbox out of the photographs. It builds the engine checkout beside it, as it is on disk | no direct link | [SpaceTrainMac/FlipperVPX](https://github.com/SpaceTrainMac/FlipperVPX) |
| [FlipperWizard](../FlipperWizard) | the wizard: the robot that plays the table with no hands on the buttons - its four layers and two stacks, the headless driver that came before it had eyes, the bench that reads what it recorded, the loop that trains it and the papers reporting what it learned. It builds the FlipperVPX checkout beside it, as it is on disk, and through it the engine | no direct link | [SpaceTrainMac/FlipperWizard](https://github.com/SpaceTrainMac/FlipperWizard) |
| [FlipperHandbooks](../FlipperHandbooks) | the toolchain that assembles five books - a player card, an operator handbook, a developer handbook, a simulator handbook and a VPX handbook - out of the repositories next door. It owns manifests, templates and generators, and no facts about the machine | no direct link | [SpaceTrainMac/FlipperHandbooks](https://github.com/SpaceTrainMac/FlipperHandbooks) |
| **FlipperWiki** | the wiki for whoever is at the glass: one page per thing a player can point at, compiled by an LLM out of rule files cut one at a time from the documents next door. The only repository here with prose of its own, and nothing under wiki/ is written by a person | **- you are here -** | [SpaceTrainMac/FlipperWiki](https://github.com/SpaceTrainMac/FlipperWiki) |
| [FlipperMaster](../FlipperMaster) | the master's thesis about the wizard, written for the Faculty of Informatics at TU Wien: the proposal, the nine chapters, the bibliography and the vendored document class. Prose about the machine and the programs beside it, and none of them in it - the figures are copied in, so it builds from this checkout alone | no direct link | [SpaceTrainMac/FlipperMaster](https://github.com/SpaceTrainMac/FlipperMaster) |
| [FlipperSounds](../FlipperSounds) | the five sound sets the engine plays, each with its own sounds.json and icon | no direct link | [SpaceTrainMac/FlipperSounds](https://github.com/SpaceTrainMac/FlipperSounds) |
| [FlipperMisc](../FlipperMisc) | the junkyard: material rather than product, that nothing in this project builds, reads or needs - two captured UART traces mcp can replay by hand, an Xcode project that will not open from a clone, a test bench that has not compiled since 2024-12-26, and somebody's scratch file | no direct link | [SpaceTrainMac/FlipperMisc](https://github.com/SpaceTrainMac/FlipperMisc) |
| [FlipperSTM](../FlipperSTM) | the STM32 firmware. Empty. Whether the firmware is one repository or two - this one, or FlipperSTM_In and FlipperSTM_Out - is undecided as of 2026-08-29 | no direct link | [SpaceTrainMac/FlipperSTM](https://github.com/SpaceTrainMac/FlipperSTM) |
| [FlipperSTM_In](../FlipperSTM_In) | the firmware for STM32-IN, which owns the switch matrix and is the only source of inbound frames. Empty, and see FlipperSTM | no direct link | [SpaceTrainMac/FlipperSTM_In](https://github.com/SpaceTrainMac/FlipperSTM_In) |
| [FlipperSTM_Out](../FlipperSTM_Out) | the firmware for STM32-OUT, which drives the lamps, coils, displays and relays. Empty, and see FlipperSTM | no direct link | [SpaceTrainMac/FlipperSTM_Out](https://github.com/SpaceTrainMac/FlipperSTM_Out) |
| FlipperEngine.org | the previous, all in one place, engine repository. It is archived, and the engine has been split into FlipperEngine and FlipperSimulator | no direct link | [SpaceTrainMac/FlipperEngine.org](https://github.com/SpaceTrainMac/FlipperEngine.org) |

**The first column is a path; the last is where it came from.** Each repository is a checkout beside this one, so `../FlipperEngine` is where FlipperEngine is - on whatever branch you have it on, and that is what every document in this project links to. **No link anywhere here names a branch.** A row you have not cloned yet is a path that goes nowhere until you do, which is what the remote is for:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/SpaceTrainMac/<Repository>.git ../<Repository>
```

**FlipperEngine.org is archived** - nothing reads it, no setup asks you to clone it, and there is no path to it above, because a path to a checkout nobody has is dead in every copy of this table. The remote is still in the row, for the one time somebody needs to go and look.

## What else has to be on disk

| Checkout | What it is | Needed by | Remote |
|---|---|---|---|
| `../third-party/vpinball` | Visual Pinball X - the physics simulator the two plugins are built against and load into, the cabinet's from FlipperVPX and the wizard's from FlipperWizard. Somebody else's program, GPLv3+, and no repository of this project | [FlipperVPX](../FlipperVPX), [FlipperWizard](../FlipperWizard) | [vpinball](https://github.com/vpinball/vpinball.git) |

**These are not repositories of this project, and they are not in the count above.** Each one has to be on the machine before one of the rows in the first table can do its job, and nobody here wrote a line of it - the same kind of thing as a pinned compiler, and not the same kind of thing as a checkout from SpaceTrainMac. None of them reads anything of ours, which is why the column that says which way the arrow points is missing from this table: the arrow only goes one way.

**The path is where it belongs rather than where it is.** The scripts that need one of these search the older position too, so a machine that has not moved its copy keeps working, and each of them says which it found.

**And each is pinned by a witness rather than by a version number** - `FlipperVPX/vpx.origin` for vpinball. A witness records the revision the thing was last known to work against. It is not a pin, which is an equality, and not a floor, which is a minimum: the build reports how far the checkout on this machine has moved from it and gates nothing, because somebody else's push must not be able to break a build here.

**This file is generated.** `FlipperArchitecture/repositories.json` is the source, and
editing this copy by hand is a change the next run reverts. To change what it says, edit
that file and regenerate every copy:

```bash
./gen_structure.sh            # from a FlipperArchitecture checkout
./gen_structure.sh --check    # exits 1 naming any copy that has drifted
```
